title: Iraq Crude Output Hits 2019 High as Brent Tops $96, Iran Preps Zero-Oil Budget, and Germany Eyes €4B Urenco Buyout
subhead: Brent rebounded above $96 amid Middle East supply risks even as Iraqi output surged, Tehran modeled zero oil revenue, and Berlin moved to keep uranium enrichment in European hands.

sections.heading: Iraq Output Surges to 4.6 Million Bpd as Brent Climbs Above $96
sections.body:
OilPrice, citing the International Energy Agency's monthly report, reported that Iraq's crude oil production reached 4.6 million barrels per day (bpd) in October—its highest level since 2019 and up 540,000 bpd from September—alongside higher output from Kuwait and Saudi Arabia.

Even so, OilPrice noted that Brent crude climbed back above $96 a barrel as peace-deal optimism faded, while Star reported Yemen's Houthi forces claimed drone strikes against Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline and Riyadh's airport.
sections.whyItMatters: Higher Gulf production is colliding with renewed geopolitical risk premiums and direct threats to Saudi pipeline infrastructure.

sections.heading: Iran Drafts Next Year's Budget Assuming Zero Oil Revenue
sections.body:
OilPrice reported that senior Iranian budget official Mohammad Ghasemi instructed the government to prepare next year's state budget on the premise that oil revenue could fall to zero. According to the report, Iran has loaded no crude oil exports since August 25.

Meanwhile, Anadolu Agency reported that the United States and Iran traded sharp accusations over maritime security at the UN Security Council.
sections.whyItMatters: Planning for zero crude revenue signals severe fiscal strain in Tehran as export flows remain halted.

sections.heading: Germany Eyes €4 Billion Buyout of RWE and E.ON's Urenco Stake
sections.body: OilPrice, citing German media, reported that Berlin plans to acquire RWE and E.ON's one-third stake in uranium enrichment firm Urenco for up to €4 billion. The move was reportedly requested by Britain to keep ownership in European hands as the UK prepares to use Urenco to produce fuel for military nuclear reactors.
sections.whyItMatters: European governments are stepping in directly to secure sovereign control over nuclear enrichment capacity for both civilian and defense reactors.

sections.heading: Trump Extends Jones Act Waiver as US Crude Output Hits Record
sections.body:
OilPrice reported that President Donald Trump extended the Jones Act waiver for another 90 days on Friday, allowing foreign-flagged tankers to transport oil and commodities between US ports to ease fuel-cost pressures during the Iran conflict.

Separately, Baker Hughes data cited by OilPrice showed active US oil rigs held steady at 463 (with total rigs at 601) as domestic crude production hit another record, while the US Senate approved a preliminary version of the BAAJA bill affecting utility and AI data-center power competition.
sections.whyItMatters: Washington is combining maritime shipping waivers with record domestic drilling while Congress debates how to balance grid capacity between utilities and AI hyperscalers.

sections.heading: Turkey Expedites Energy Expropriations and Sets Akkuyu Timeline
sections.body: Ekonomim reported that Turkey authorized urgent expropriations across six provinces—Ankara, Konya, Kahramanmaraş, Kırıkkale, Çorum, and Mersin—for power transmission lines and natural gas distribution infrastructure. Separately, Rosatom CEO Alexey Likhachev outlined the timeline for first electricity generation at the Akkuyu Nuclear Power Plant.
sections.whyItMatters: Ankara is fast-tracking grid and gas distribution buildouts alongside preparations for its first nuclear power generation.

bottomLine: Brent's rebound above $96, Iran's zero-oil budget planning, and Germany's €4 billion Urenco move show energy markets simultaneously pricing active Middle East supply threats and state intervention in nuclear and maritime fuel logistics.
